sections.h2: Who sends the Manatee County property tax bill?
sections.html:
Two Manatee County offices split the job: the property appraiser sets the value and the tax collector sends and collects the bill. The collector's own overview says the appraiser mails the TRIM notice each year and the collector mails the tax bill, then passes the money on to the local taxing authorities.

That split matters when you plan a sale. A question about an exemption, a parcel record or an assessed value goes to the Manatee County Property Appraiser. A question about what is owed, which discount applies or whether a certificate has been issued goes to the Manatee County Tax Collector. The clerk of court, at manateeclerk.com, keeps the Official Records where deeds and liens are recorded.

  • Property appraiser: parcel search, homestead e-filing, tangible personal property returns, TRIM notices, value reviews and Value Adjustment Board information.
  • Tax collector: bills, payments, installment plans, delinquent accounts and the annual tax certificate sale.
  • Clerk: recorded deeds, mortgages and liens, plus tax deed sales run for the county.

sections.h2: When do Manatee County property taxes have to be paid?
sections.html:
Manatee County bills go out in early November and the full amount is due by March 31, with a discount for paying early. The tax collector's page describes the 2026 roll as opening for collection with the November 2 mailing of 220,594 annual bills and informational notices.

The collector prints a month-by-month discount schedule, shown below for the 2026 bills. It also states that payments must arrive in person by 5:00 p.m., or be postmarked or paid online by 11:59 p.m., on the deadline day.

Discount periods for annual payment of 2026 Manatee County bills, as printed by the Tax Collector
Payment windowDiscount
November 2 to December 34%
December 4 to December 313%
January 1 to January 312%
February 1 to February 281%
March 1 to March 31No discount, last day before delinquency

Florida's revenue department describes the same early-payment ladder and says unpaid taxes turn delinquent on April 1.

sections.h2: Can Manatee County owners pay in installments?
sections.html:
Yes. Under section 197.222 of the Florida Statutes, the tax collector offers a plan of four quarterly payments, and the prior year's taxes must have exceeded $100 to join. State guidance puts the application deadline at May 1 of the assessment year.

The Manatee installment page lists these deadlines and discounts:

  • June 30, first installment: 6% discount. A first installment paid by July 31 earns no discount.
  • September 30, second installment: 4.5% discount.
  • December 31, third installment: 3% discount.
  • March 31, fourth installment: no discount, and the last day before delinquency.

If you plan to list or sell during the plan year, tell the collector, because a payoff at closing has to settle whatever remains on the bill.

sections.h2: What happens if Manatee County taxes are not paid?
sections.html:
Taxes unpaid after March 31 become delinquent on April 1 and can pick up fees, interest and collection costs. The collector adds that after April 1 payments must be received by the last business day of the month, and postmarks are not accepted.

Florida's revenue department says certificates are sold on all unpaid items by June 1. The Manatee collector confirms that its office holds an annual sale and issues a certificate against the property when taxes remain unpaid on or before June 1, and that paying the taxes cancels the certificate. Certificates that nobody buys at the sale default to the county, and investors can buy those later from the county-held list.

A certificate is not a deed. Under section 197.502, a holder can apply for a tax deed after two years have passed since April 1 of the year the certificate was issued, and the tax collector then lists the owner, lienholders and any contract-for-deed buyer to be notified. A homestead property carries a higher opening bid, because one-half of the latest assessed value is added.

sections.h2: What exemptions and caps apply in Manatee County?
sections.html:
Manatee homeowners use the same state exemptions as every Florida county, filed with the county property appraiser. Homestead applies to a permanent residence you owned and lived in on January 1, and the paperwork is Form DR-501, due March 1. The appraiser's site offers an electronic filing option.

  • Homestead exemption: up to $50,000, with the first $25,000 applying to all taxes including school taxes and the second $25,000 applying to value over $50,000 for non-school taxes.
  • Save Our Homes: once homesteaded, yearly growth in assessed value is limited to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change. The state's chart lists a 2.7% cap for 2026.
  • Non-homestead property: assessed value may rise no more than 10 percent a year.
  • Portability: a new homestead must be established within three years of January 1 of the year the old one was given up, with Form DR-501T filed alongside the application.
  • Tax deferral: Form DR-570 goes to the tax collector by March 31 for eligible homesteads.

A sale counts as a change of ownership, so the property returns to just value on the following January 1 for the next owner. Homestead ends once the home is rented or is no longer your permanent residence.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Manatee County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the TRIM notice that the property appraiser mails in August, then ask the appraiser's office for a review of the value. The appraiser's homepage lists a request-a-review option for owners who think the assessed value is wrong, plus a page on the Value Adjustment Board.

A formal challenge goes to the clerk of the court. The state's revenue department sets a petition deadline of 25 days from the date of the Notice of Proposed Property Taxes, using one of the DR-486 forms. A denied exemption or classification has a separate 30-day window counted from the mailing of the denial letter. Read the dates on your own notice, since they are tied to its mailing.

Owners with a tangible personal property account on January 1 must file a return with the appraiser by April 1 each year, and the appraiser offers a 30-day extension request.

sections.h2: How are Manatee County taxes handled when you sell a house?
sections.html:
Selling with an open Manatee bill is workable: the closing agent can settle it out of what the buyer pays. Request a payoff figure from the title company and the account status from the collector. Taxes are due even if a bill never reached you, and a certificate on the parcel has to be redeemed before clean title passes.

Florida's deed stamp tax is 70 cents per $100 of consideration under section 201.02, and all parties to the document are liable regardless of who agrees to pay. The clerk takes the tax at the moment the deed goes on record. Selling to a cash buyer does not remove any of these items. It only changes how quickly the closing can happen, because no lender appraisal or underwriting is involved.

Where back taxes, a certificate or a tax deed application already sits on the parcel, get the exact amount in writing from the collector before a closing date is fixed.

sections.h2: Does the tax bill change after a Manatee County sale?
sections.html:
Yes. A sale ends any Save Our Homes cap the seller built up, so the next owner's assessment resets to just value the following January 1. Do not use the seller's current bill to estimate what a buyer will pay.

The property appraiser publishes preliminary rolls, reports and prior-year millage on its site. Use them to look up the parcel and its millage history. For the millage rate on one address, ask the collector or appraiser, since each taxing authority sets its own.

faqs.q: Who answers questions about a Manatee County tax bill?
faqs.a: The Manatee County Tax Collector handles bills, payments, installments and delinquent accounts. The property appraiser handles values and exemptions, and the clerk handles recorded deeds and liens.

faqs.q: Is there a discount for paying Manatee County property tax early?
faqs.a: Yes. The collector's schedule for the 2026 bills gives 4% from November 2 to December 3, 3% from December 4 to December 31, 2% in January and 1% in February. March has no discount.

faqs.q: When do Manatee County taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: They become delinquent on April 1. The tax collector then sells tax certificates on unpaid parcels in an annual sale held on or before June 1, and paying the taxes cancels a certificate.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Manatee County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid amount is usually settled from your proceeds at closing. Ask the title company for the payoff and confirm any certificate with the tax collector.

faqs.q: When must I apply for a homestead exemption in Manatee County?
faqs.a: Apply to the Manatee County Property Appraiser by the March 1 deadline. The home must be your permanent residence as of January 1, and the appraiser accepts electronic filing.
